The first part is to do text preprocessing in order to extract the numeric data from the calls and the second is classification using machine learning algorithms.

This research paper introduces a review of different text categorization techniques that can be used for the text classification task of call routing. Specifically, we focus on the text pre-processing techniques and machine learning classification methods which are used in this task. The review will help to understand what text categories are suitable for different kinds of calls and how these categories can be used in automatic routing.

The review starts by explaining the importance of the pre-processing part and why it should be treated separately from the classifying part. Next, the review presents some methods which are commonly used to extract the text features and how these methods affect the text classification results. The review also presents some common machine learning approaches that can be used in the classifying stage.
The review also gives a critical discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of the different methods. A conclusion is drawn that the text pre-processing and classifying method selection depend on the particular problem at hand.

Purpose – The purpose of this study is to explore the causal link between procurement route and the ongoing buyer-supplier relationship.

Design/methodology/approach – The research draws on literature in the areas of: facilities management (FM) outsourcing; purchasing and supply chain management; relationship marketing; and service operations to provide a theoretical basis for the study. This research is conducted through a case study approach with secondary sources from the relevant literature as well as interviews with 21 FM procurement managers.

Findings – The results of this research show that the FM procuring organisation and its chosen supplier have had the best performance when buying from external suppliers, although both parties may suffer if the supplier is internal. The main reason why this might happen is that it could not be proved that the internal suppliers will work towards the same strategy of the procuring organisation or that they can work in a flexible way to fit the needs of the organization.

Research limitations/implications – This research is limited to FM procurement. Further research should be carried out for FM maintenance, FM management services and other fields.

Practical implications – There is some practical implication which is that FM procuring organisations should consider to buy from suppliers who do not have any relation with the procuring organizations.

Originality/value – This research provides an original contribution to the literature as there has been no prior research into the effects of procurement route on ongoing relations in FM procurement.

generations.raw_text: The widespread availability of many emerging services enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm passes through the capability to provide long-range connectivity to a massive number of things, overcoming the well-known issues of ad-hoc, short-range networks. This requires a large-scale network capable of supporting millions of devices, which is known as a cellular network. The support of such traffic in current cellular networks is not enough due to the low capacity and small coverage area. In this study, we analyzed a new technology, called the Fifth-Generation Cellular Network (5G), which is able to support the massive machine-to-machine (M2M) traffic thanks to its higher capacity than the existing fourth-generation network (4G), and also has an important role on supporting the huge number of mobile things, thanks to its huge coverage area. The result of our research proves that 5G cellular network is a candidate to support the massive M2M traffic.

GHz third harmonic superconducting cavities have been used to increase the peak bunch current and to compensate for non-linear distortions in the longitudinal phase space due to sinusoidal 1.3 GHz accelerating cavity voltage (1). The power coupler for the 3.9 GHz superconducting cavity at Fermilab plays an important role in transferring the energy from the input line into the cavity, which affects the performance of the particle accelerator. In this study, we investigated the properties of the new 3.9 GHz power coupler for the superconducting cavity, which has a new design that enables us to reduce the amount of RF power lost while transmitting it, and to obtain a large fraction of it into the superconducting cavity without causing damage to the structure. The optimization method of the power coupler was developed in this simulation process, where several different parameters including the shape of the input line, length of the power coupler, and the material of the power coupler were optimized. The simulation results show that the new optimized power coupler can improve the efficiency of the superconducting cavity and reduce the cost of the power coupler at the same time.

References:
(1) S. A. Danilenko et al., "Optimization of the Coupling Structures of Superconducting Cavities in Accelerators," *Physical Review Special Topics - Accelerators and Beams*, vol. 18, no. 3, pp. 030002, 2015.

generations.raw_text: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) is a principal mechanism that targets ER-associated proteins for cytosolic proteasomal degradation. Here, our data demonstrate a critical role for the SEL1L-HRD1 and SEL1L-HSP70/40 hetero-complexes in managing an important checkpoint in B cell development. We have demonstrated that the SEL1L-HRD1 complex is involved in the removal of misfolded proteins from the ER lumen via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. Our experiments were conducted on two murine models: a humanized 2B1 model and a Sel1l-/- model, both undergoing a B cell developmental process from pro-B cells to mature B cells. We found that mice deficient for SEL1L/HSP70 or SEL1L/HSP40 fail to make a transition from pro-B cells to pre-B cells. We further showed that the expression level of the BCR component Igα is down-regulated at the pre-B cell stage in SEL1L-deficient 2B1 mice. Using biochemical affinity purification, we identified Ufd1 as one of the substrates of SEL1L-HSP70 or SEL1L-HSP40. Moreover, we found that UFD1 is down-expressed and cleaved in the absence of SEL1L in B cells. These results suggest that SEL1L and the other two components play a key role in regulating the transition from the pro-B to the pre-B stage through a specific mechanism that removes the UFD1 protein via the cytosolic protein degradation system.
